title: Trade Marks Act s. 25 — Statutory provision (Trade Marks Act s. 25)

content.overview: Section 25 fixes the registration term at ten years, renewable for further ten-year periods on application and fee. A mark not renewed is removed. Restoration is possible within the enacted further period. The right lasts while the registration is renewed.
content.glance: Trade Marks Act s. 25 — Statutory provision (Trade Marks Act s. 25). Complete IPR treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective and Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body:
Trade Marks Act s. 25 — Statutory provision (Trade Marks Act s. 25) sits within Intellectual Property Rights and is governed by Copyright Act, 1957; Trade Marks Act, 1999; Patents Act, 1970; Designs Act, 2000; Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999 and allied rules.

cases.name: R.G. Anand v. Deluxe Films
cases.facts: The dispute concerned alleged copying of a dramatic work into a film.
cases.issue: What test determines substantial copyright infringement of an idea or expression.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Copyright protects expression, not ideas, and infringement depends on substantial similarity assessed from the work as a whole.
cases.holding: The Court stated the governing comparison test.
cases.relevance: Use for copyright infringement and idea-expression distinction.

cases.name: Novartis AG v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Court considered patentability of a pharmaceutical form under s. 3(d).
cases.issue: What enhanced efficacy threshold applies to a pharmaceutical derivative.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 3(d) requires the statutory enhanced-efficacy threshold and prevents evergreening without the required proof.
cases.holding: The patent claim was rejected under the statutory standard.
cases.relevance: Use for patentability exclusions and pharmaceutical patents.

cases.name: Cadila Health Care Ltd. v. Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd.
cases.facts: The parties used similar marks for pharmaceutical products.
cases.issue: How should deceptive similarity be assessed in pharmaceutical trademark disputes.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts must apply a stricter likelihood-of-confusion test for medicines because confusion may endanger public health.
cases.holding: The Court directed a careful comparison of the marks and circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for trademark confusion and public-interest analysis.

enhancement.definition: Section 25 fixes the registration term at ten years, renewable for further ten-year periods on application and fee. A mark not renewed is removed. Restoration is possible within the enacted further period.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The right lasts while the registration is renewed.
essentialIngredients: Restoration only in the further period
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Renewal may be filed in the period before expiry the rules state. Removal follows non-renewal. A removed mark can be restored if the proprietor applies within the statutory further time and shows the enacted cause. Use requirements are a separate rectification ground.
enhancement.examples: A registration granted in 2016 is renewed in 2026. Without renewal it is removed. A renewal five years late is outside the ordinary restoration window.
enhancement.problemApplication: Match the facts to the section before using a neighbouring right. Do not invent a case ratio.
